interface.title: Western Flyer - CTD (SBE 19plus V2)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploring, quality-checking and exporting CTD casts that have already been processed
interface.what_it_is_for: Browse a ship's processed CTD casts by cruise and station: depth profiles, T-S diagrams, along-track sections with density contours, mixed-layer depth, AOU and metabolic index, a per-station health table, and a CSV export that follows the current filters.

data.note: Four cruises are already loaded from the DuckDB file: 2025_Baja (26 casts), 2025_MontereyBay (15 casts, WF #6 missing, the removed deck-test cast), 2026_MontereyBay (not opened by the explorer; the replay saw only its Station ID list, SC1_Cast1…C1_Cast10) and 2026_PNW (5 casts). Esri basemap tiles never loaded on the Geolocation map, so station dots sit on a blank background.

tree.general: Explore, quality-check and extract measurements from a set of vertical sensor casts taken on several survey trips
tree.specific: Explore Western Flyer SBE19plus CTD casts by cruise and station, check QC, and export the binned data

features.name: Cascading survey/site picker driving the per-site views
features.general: Pick a survey, then a site from a list that refreshes for that survey; the per-site plots, table and export switch to that selection
features.specific: The Cruise ID dropdown refills Station ID (after a short delay); the single-station tabs (profiles, multi-axis, T-S, MLD, AOU, Metabolic Index, Tabular Data) and Export CSV follow the pair. Cruise Summary and Vertical Section follow Cruise ID only
steps: choose a cruise in Cruise ID
Station ID list repopulates with that cruise's casts
choose a station
any open per-station tab redraws for that station
serves_tasks: Choose a survey and see its list of sites refresh
View every measured variable against depth for one cast
Plot temperature against salinity, coloured by depth, for one site and then another

features.name: Station map with selected-site highlight
features.general: Map of a survey's sites with the current site highlighted and a hover read-out of position and name
features.specific: Geolocation tab: station dots, a large red dot for the selected Station ID, hover shows lon/lat/station_id. Clicking a dot does not select it; the Esri basemap did not load
steps: open Geolocation
hover a dot to read lon, lat and station_id
choose a station in Station ID
the red highlight moves to that station
serves_tasks: Find where each site lies and which one is selected

features.name: QC-flag and warm-up filters with depth window
features.general: Two on/off filters (drop flagged points, include the instrument warm-up segment) plus a two-handle depth range, applied to the per-site plots, table and export
features.specific: Filter QC (Flag < 3), Show Soak Data (Surface) and the Depth Range (m) range slider. The Vertical Section uses only Depth Range and Filter QC (soak bins always left out); Cruise Summary and Geolocation ignore all three
steps: drag Depth Range handles to a window (e.g. 0..63 m)
tick Show Soak Data to add the 0-10 m soak bins
tick or untick Filter QC to drop or keep flag-3 bins
compare the redrawn profiles or table rows
serves_tasks: See how removing flagged points changes a profile
Show or hide the instrument's warm-up period at the surface
Limit the plots to a depth window
Download the current site's data, with the current filters applied, as a spreadsheet file

features.name: Per-site health table
features.general: A sortable table of sampling events with location, time, maximum depth and a bar-coded quality percentage, for ranking sites by data quality
features.specific: Cruise Summary table: Station ID, WF #, SB #, Lat, Lon, Start Time, Max Depth (m), Health % (share of the cast's bins with qc_flag = 1) shown as a bar
steps: open Cruise Summary
click the Health % header to sort ascending
read the lowest-health casts at the top
spot gaps in WF # (e.g. cast 6 missing in 2025_MontereyBay)
serves_tasks: Rank sites by a data-quality score to find the weakest ones

features.name: Side-by-side depth profile panels
features.general: Several variable-versus-depth panels sharing one inverted depth axis, so features line up across variables
features.specific: Vertical Profiles: Pot. Temp, In-Situ Temp, Prac. Sal, O2, pH, Chl with linked pan/zoom/hover toolbar
steps: select a station
open Vertical Profiles
narrow the depth range to zoom on the upper layer
toggle QC and soak to compare shapes
serves_tasks: View every measured variable against depth for one cast
See how removing flagged points changes a profile

features.name: Multi-axis overlay profile with toggleable legend
features.general: Overlay several variables on one depth plot, each with its own stacked x-axis, and hide series by clicking the legend
features.specific: Multi-Axis Profile: pH, Oxygen, Salinity, In-Situ Temp, Chlorophyll on separate top and bottom axes
steps: open Multi-Axis Profile
read each colour against its own axis
click a legend entry to mute that series
serves_tasks: Overlay several variables on one depth axis

features.name: Property-property scatter coloured by depth
features.general: Scatter two measured properties against each other, coloured by depth, with box zoom and hover read-out of the derived density
features.specific: T-S Analysis (EOS-80): theta vs SP coloured by depth_m; hover shows SP, theta, depth_m, sigma
steps: select a station
open T-S Analysis
Box Zoom into a cluster
hover points to read sigma
Reset, then switch station to compare
serves_tasks: Plot temperature against salinity, coloured by depth, for one site and then another

features.name: Along-track section with variable picker
features.general: Interpolate all sites of a survey into a distance-by-depth colour section for a chosen variable, with density contour lines and site markers, then zoom, hover and save the image
features.specific: Vertical Section: Section Variable dropdown (7 variables), colour section vs Distance Along Track (km) built from all the cruise's casts in time order, σθ isopycnal contours every 0.5 kg/m³ (unchanged when the variable changes), station triangles, Bokeh pan/box zoom/save. Uses Cruise ID, Depth Range and Filter QC; ignores Station ID and always leaves out soak bins
steps: open Vertical Section
choose a Section Variable
hover to read distance, depth, value
Box Zoom into a region (e.g. the chlorophyll maximum)
Save to PNG
serves_tasks: View an interpolated distance-by-depth cross-section of a chosen variable along the survey track

features.name: Mixed-layer depth marker on density profile
features.general: Plot density against depth with a computed mixed-layer depth line
features.specific: Stability & MLD: sigma vs depth_m with a red MLD line; Oxygen Concentration area plot alongside
steps: select a station
open Stability & MLD
read the MLD line against the density gradient
serves_tasks: Find the depth of the well-mixed surface layer

features.name: Derived oxygen-deficit and habitat-index profiles
features.general: Profile a derived oxygen deficit against the saturation curve, and a metabolic habitat index against its viability threshold, each against depth
features.specific: Oxygen Utilization (AOU): Observed O2, dashed Sat. Cap line and AOU shaded area (misdrawn: hugs Sat. Cap rather than filling between observed and saturation, code line 299). Metabolic Index: Φ vs depth with a dashed Φ=1 line (per code)
steps: select a station
scroll the tab bar right and open Oxygen Utilization (AOU)
compare the observed curve with the saturation line
open Metabolic Index
read Φ against the Φ=1 threshold
serves_tasks: Look at derived oxygen-deficit and metabolic habitat-suitability measures against depth

features.name: Filtered table with CSV export
features.general: Page through the selected site's binned rows with quality flags, then download the filtered rows as CSV
features.specific: Tabular Data (paged, sortable, scrollable) plus the Export CSV sidebar button writing CTD_Export.csv
steps: open Tabular Data
page and scroll to the qc_flag / is_soak columns
set the QC and soak filters
press Export CSV
the CSV follows the QC and soak settings (whether it follows Depth Range was not checked)
serves_tasks: Inspect the binned rows with their quality flags
Download the current site's data, with the current filters applied, as a spreadsheet file

screens_never_reached: Per-cruise build provenance (calibration SHA-256, git commit, rows written): not shown anywhere in the dashboard. The Cruise Summary tab has only the station table (screens/003.webp).
Geolocation basemap: Esri tiles never loaded (only the attribution text shows), so stations appear on a blank background (screens/009.webp).
Isopycnal contours on the T-S diagram: the T-S Analysis tab shows only the scatter, with no density contours (screens/038.webp, screens/055.webp).
not_done: Checking build provenance (calibration SHA-256, git commit, rows written): the interface has no view for it.
Comparing several stations on one T-S diagram: the T-S tab plots only the selected station, so the comparison was done by switching stations one at a time.

2026_MontereyBay was not opened by the explorer, so its README-documented issues went unprobed: the split pH calibration window, the duplicate sb_cast 10, and the overlapping C1/MossLandingCanyon markers.
Clicking a map dot (screens/011.webp) or a Cruise Summary row (screens/006.webp, row only highlights) does not select that station; selection works only through the Station ID dropdown.
The theme toggle reloads the page with ?theme=dark and resets cruise, depth range and filters to their defaults (screens/067.webp). Dark mode was seen but not explored further.
The Φ profile was not read against its Φ=1 threshold line; the Metabolic Index tab was only opened (screens/044.webp).
Whether Export CSV respects the Depth Range was not checked; only the QC and soak settings were compared in the files.

Interpolation looks questionable in places: the 2026_PNW section joins the Oregon shelf casts and Marrowstone Island across about 400 km, since it strings all the cruise's casts in time order (screens/059.webp). The AOU shading hugs the Sat. Cap line around 250-300 µmol/kg instead of filling between observed O2 and saturation (screens/043.webp; the reviewer traced it to code line 299).
